locator.text: Equation (7.18), p. 79, in the proof of Proposition 7.2

evidence: paper: V_m(v, w) \;=\; \exp\Bigl(-(m^2 - 1)\int_w^v d(a)\, da\Bigr)\, V_1(v, w) .

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The paper's exact factorisation of the fundamental matrix is not in the repository: no declaration was found that introduces a solution operator or fundamental matrix V_m(v, w) at all, so the identity V_m = exp(-(m²-1)∫_w^v d) V_1 is not stated. The Lean reaches the conclusion the paper draws from (7.18) — that the propagator bound (7.19) holds for every harmonic m ≠ 0 with the constants of m = 1 — by an energy/Grönwall route on the solutions themselves instead: high_harmonic_damping is the scalar inequality d - δ ≤ j²D for j ≠ 0 (i.e. extra harmonics only add damping), and high_harmonic_propagator_estimate feeds it into the same growth estimate used for the single harmonic, with no factorisation of a matrix. This is a different formula and a different route, not a weaker conclusion for the use the paper makes of it; severity low because the surrounding uniform-in-m propagator bound is still obtained. I did not check whether (7.18) is used anywhere in the paper for anything beyond that uniformity.
